testing_note: Wrote a scratch case (empty CSV export ticket with a customer-claimed uptime promise, an agent's unauthorised credit promise, a P2 policy in business hours with an EU region but no exact time zone) and walked the steps by hand. Changes: removed an invented 'at risk' threshold (25% of window) since it was itself a made-up service-level term, replacing it with met/open/breached/cannot determine plus any policy-defined status; added the rule that a status identical under every plausible value of a missing term may be given with the term named; added a policy note beside commitments that the policy limits (credits only via Account Management); made customer-attributed promises explicitly [reported] claims; allowed one service-level block per clock.
applied_note: I made it a model-invoked skill with a short description that front-loads the leading words 'escalation handoff' and carries one trigger branch, and kept it in a single file because every case needs the tags, steps and template (no branch justified disclosure). The reported/verified distinction rides on co-located provenance tags used as leading words throughout, each step ends on a checkable, exhaustive completion criterion, and the no-invention rules are phrased positively (every line traces to a source; a commitment exists only where the thread's words made it; missing terms are named) and enforced by a final trace pass.
